title: The Castle Toilet That Let an Army In
description:
Castle toilets were called garderobes: tiny rooms on the outer wall with a stone seat, and a chute that dropped straight down the outside of the wall, often into the moat. In 1204, French soldiers were besieging Château Gaillard, one of the strongest castles in Europe. Accounts say a few men climbed up a latrine chute, got inside and let their army in. Later castles added bars and bends to their chutes.

Would you have climbed it?

Sources: World History Encyclopedia, "Toilets in a Medieval Castle"; Siege of Château Gaillard (1203–1204), overview of the accounts; Kaufmann & Kaufmann, The Medieval Fortress. Details of the climb differ between accounts.
